item.title: Why potluck parties are making a big comeback in America
item.description:
Communities across the United States are fighting loneliness by sharing meals together. On July fifth, an initiative called America’s Potluck led people across all fifty states to mark the country’s semiquincentennial. The America two hundred fifty Utah Commission organized the event. More than seventeen hundred communities took part across the country. In the Trenton, New Jersey neighborhood of Hiltonia, about twenty-five residents gathered for a potluck. Revolution NJ helped organize that gathering. Participant, Thomas Emerick said that people will always show up if you feed them.
Americans are eating alone much more often than before. In twenty twenty-three, about one in four adults reported eating all their meals alone the previous day. That is a fifty-three percent rise since two thousand three. Research highlights the social toll and benefits of these dining habits. The twenty twenty-five World Happiness Report found a strong link between sharing meals and higher subjective well-being. A report from the Foundation for Social Connection points to food as a force for building social ties.
Groups such as Community Plate in Maine have hosted more than fifty gatherings since its first supper in Lubec in twenty twenty-three. Surveys of nearly four hundred participants found that ninety-six percent made ties with someone they did not know well. Eighty-eight percent felt more connected to their community afterward., Karl Schatz cofounded Community Plate. He noted that food connects us to our family histories and our communities.
Food historians note that potlucks have long served as an ancient social form for pooling resources. They create a sense of common care outside of family structures., Karl Schatz described the dynamic of sharing dishes. When people bring food and feed each other, a simultaneous giving and receiving takes place. That creates a sense of both helping and being helped.

item.title: Extreme pressure turns blue pigment into record-long single-atom copper chains
item.description: Scientists have made record-long single-atom copper chains. They used extreme pressure on a common blue pigment. This could lead to microscopic molecular wires. Traditional silicon chips are reaching their physical limits. Researchers used copper phthalocyanine crystals. This is the base for phthalo blue. They put the crystals inside a diamond anvil cell. They applied pressures exceeding twenty-one gigapascals. That is roughly two hundred thousand times normal atmospheric pressure. This high-pressure solid-state reaction bypassed traditional liquid-solution limits. Those older methods usually stop when chemical wrappers become insoluble. They normally yield chains shorter than ten atoms. The new structure features more than four thousand copper atoms. They form a single chain stretching for micrometers. This is two to three orders of magnitude longer than the old record of twenty-eight atoms. Each nanowire cable forms a three-layer structure. It has a copper atomic core. It has a conductive ring-like frame of carbon and nitrogen atoms. It has an outer protective s-p-three-carbon network sheath. This sheath locks the chain into a stable line. Computer models and measurements were published in Science. They showed that electricity flows more than ten times faster along the wire than sideways in real-world samples. The surrounding carbon and nitrogen framework carries the current. The weakly bonded copper atoms do not carry it. The wires proved stable in air. They survived hours in an acidic solution under harsh ultrasonic vibrations. The requirement of extreme pressure presents a bottleneck. This could hinder industrial-scale production.

item.title: Everton v Manchester United: Premier League – live
item.description: Hackney shimmies through the number ten zone and slips the ball rightwards to George. George takes a touch and then blasts the ball past Lammens. This leaves more gaps for a United side whose build up was often too leisurely in the first half.

item.title: Delhi University Students’ Union campaigner recalls pulling students from Satya Niketan building collapse rubble
item.description:
Krishna Bhardwaj, a first responder from Gwalior in Madhya Pradesh who was in Delhi campaigning for the D. U. S. U. elections, was among those who rushed to the site after a building collapsed on Sunday, September sixth, twenty twenty-six.
Bhardwaj and a team of twenty-five to thirty members arrived before police and fire personnel, rescuing four people.
During one rescue attempt, a rescued student pleaded to Krishna Bhardwaj by saying, Bhaiyya, please mujhe bacha lo.
During the operation, Bhardwaj sustained a foot injury from a falling stone while removing a body and was taken to the hospital for treatment.
He noted that seven students had been shifted to the hospital while casualties were still being assessed, and alleged that many area buildings are unauthorised and operate on fake N. O. C.s.
Dal Bahadur, a local music shop owner, stated that the building had remained closed for nearly two years before reopening about a year ago.
He added that work had been underway in the basement for the past two months with trucks carrying away excavated mud and stones.
Dhruv Singh Bhatia, a third-year Motilal Nehru College student, had visited the building two days prior to check on first-year students.
He stated that thirty to thirty-five students lived in the cramped structure, with three to four students in one room-kitchen setup.
He also noted damp walls, a narrow entry, and ongoing basement work for commercial purposes accompanied by accumulated water.

item.title: Boox’s tiny Picco e-reader should land in November
item.description:
Boox announced that its new pocket-sized e-reader, the Picco, is expected to launch in November. This follows an initial teaser in July. Reporting from the I. F. A. trade show revealed new hardware details about the device. Pricing has not yet been disclosed.
The Picco features a three point nine seven inch touchscreen e-paper display. The Verge writer Andrew Liszewski called it a welcome upgrade.
Unlike competing devices such as Xteink readers, the Picco does not include magnets on the back for phone attachment. For navigation, the device is equipped with physical page-turn buttons. These buttons support customizable actions for both short and long presses.
The device has no onboard storage. It relies entirely on a micro S. D. card.

item.title: Jamaican delegates arrive in UK to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles
item.description:
Jamaican delegates arrived in the United Kingdom over the weekend. They are led by culture minister Olivia Grange and members of the National Council on Reparations. They plan to hand a landmark petition to King Charles on Monday.
Jamaica established the first Caribbean national reparations mechanism in two thousand and nine. The goal is to address the enduring impacts of slavery.
The petition was first announced in June of last year. It asks the monarch to use his authority to request legal advice. The advice will come from the London-based privy council. The questions focus on whether the forced transport of Africans to Jamaica was lawful. They also ask if it constituted a crime against humanity. Finally, they ask if Britain is obligated to provide restitution.
Grange stated that between the fifteenth and nineteenth centuries, more than twelve point five million Africans were kidnapped. They were forcibly transported to the Americas and sold into slavery. This left former colonies at a severe economic disadvantage. That disadvantage impedes their ability to tackle modern issues like the climate crisis.
Grange spoke to the Guardian regarding inherited systemic problems. She noted that we still have a lot of work to do. She added that people can imagine how much better they could have done without those inherited problems and the legacy that came out of slavery.
This visit precedes several major events. There is a Caribbean reparations conference in Barbados later this month. There is advocacy at the United Nations general assembly in late September. There is also the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua in November.
A palace spokesperson noted that King Charles has repeatedly expressed a commitment to promoting greater understanding of slavery. He also wants to address historic wrongs.

item.title: "Ready to talk": German far-right celebrates victory
item.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany party is celebrating a victory in Saxony-Anhalt as polls close. State leader Ulrich Siegmund is polling in pole position to potentially become the state leader. This success would mark the first time Germany has a far-right state since the Second World War. German intelligence agencies have designated elements of the A. F. D. as right-wing extremist. This has prompted other political parties to establish a firewall known as the Brandmauer to isolate them. The party has shifted its approach from aggressive slogans to a more positive campaign mantra. This change happened under, Ulrich Siegmund. Der Spiegel magazine labelled him Germany's most dangerous man. They called him a quote-friendly seducer masking a radical programme. Ulrich Siegmund dismissed the magazine label as a typical establishment set-up and fake P. R.

item.title: Ødegaard fires winner as Arsenal complete comeback win over Chelsea
item.description:
Chelsea took the lead after seventy-seven seconds. Morgan Rogers scored with a volley from the edge of the area. This followed a free-kick taken by Reece James. Rogers joined Chelsea for one hundred seventeen million pounds over the summer. Arsenal previously had an eighty million pound bid rejected by Aston Villa. Arsenal responded with intense pressure. This pressure culminated in an equaliser on twenty-five minutes. Kai Havertz drifted across the edge of the area. He hit a low left-foot shot past former Arsenal goalkeeper, Emiliano Martínez.
Martin Ødegaard scored shortly after half-time. He finished after a stunning dummy by Havertz. The play started from a low cross from the left by, Christos Tzolis. This victory continued Arsenal's perfect start to their title defense. They now have three wins from three games. The result extends Arsenal's unbeaten run against their cross-town rivals. That run is now eleven matches in all competitions. It includes eight wins.
Chelsea pushed for an equaliser late in the game. They forced goalkeeper, David Raya, to tip over a searing drive. That shot came from substitute, Estêvão, in the eighty-ninth minute. Arsenal maintained their advantage to secure the victory.

item.title: Small molecular substitutions reshape energy pathways behind aggregation-induced emission
item.description: Researchers at the Institute of Science Tokyo have built a new computer-guided framework. It predicts how molecules glow when they clump together. The team was led by, Associate Professor Gen-ichi Konishi. They used a small number of energy descriptors from quantum chemistry calculations. The scientists proposed that this glowing behavior comes from large structural changes in molecules. Their study was published in the journal Advanced Science. The title is, Computation-Guided Control of Excited-State Deactivation. The paper shows how adding donor and acceptor groups changes the energy surfaces of molecules. Controlling where these groups sit regulates access to conical intersections. To test their idea, the team analyzed thirty stilbene derivatives. They then built four representative bridged stilbenes in a lab. The physical properties of these four compounds matched the computer predictions. This method moves material design away from trial and error. According to, Konishi, the work shifts design toward rational and computer-guided exploration. The researchers expect the strategy to help build better organic light-emitting diodes, fluorescent probes for bioimaging, and sensing materials.

item.title: U.S. Energy Secretary Wright says Iran nuclear deal may never happen
item.description:
United States Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Sunday that the nation might not reach a deal to stop Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. This comes as their conflict enters its seventh month. The United States may instead focus on destroying Iranian capabilities to build a weapon. Wright told C. B. S. that President Donald Trump always prefers a negotiated settlement. Trump wants to avoid a military solution unless it is absolutely necessary. Wright added that the biggest role of the military right now is stopping the export of Iranian crude oil. This strategy aims to strangle the Iranian economy.
These remarks follow United States Central Command strikes. The strikes permanently disabled one Iranian crude oil carrier off the coast of Kharg Island. Another carrier was disabled near Jask, and a third tanker was attacked in the Gulf of Oman. C. E. N. T. C. O. M. stated the attacks were retaliation for ballistic missiles. Those missiles were launched by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps toward two Navy warships. The warships successfully evaded the attacks with no United States casualties. Admiral Brad Cooper warned the I. R. G. C. that the nation will impose a higher economic cost. He said the United States will take out three Iranian ships if they shoot at two American ships.
The conflict began on February twenty-eighth with American and Israeli airstrikes. A United States blockade on Iranian oil exports started in mid-April. That blockade has effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz and sent global energy prices soaring. In response to recent attacks, Iranian parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said Iran proportionate responses are over. He warned on Telegram that any violation of Iranian interests will receive a faster and heavier response. Ghalibaf acknowledged severe economic pressures facing the country. He noted that severe fluctuations in exchange rates, inflation, unemployment, and market management have put serious pressure on the people.

item.title: Fact check: Election fraud claims spread in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description:
On Sunday, Saxony-Anhalt held a consequential election. The far-right Alternative for Germany won a decisive lead. This positions the party to potentially form the first far-right state government since World War Two. In the days before the vote, false and misleading claims seized on the election importance. Social media users alleged fraud, vote-rigging, and irregularities.
A staged video viewed ten thousand times on X falsely claimed to show election workers destroying ballots for the A. F. D. The footage showed a man drawing black X marks on ballots. All contained the same name and missed the regulatory hole punch for visually impaired voters. The Russian disinformation watchdog group, the Gnida Project, identified the clip as part of the Storm-dash-fifteen-sixteen campaign controlled by Russia military intelligence agency, the G. R. U.
A separate Russian disinfo initiative dubbed Matryoshka, also known as Operation Overload, utilized spoofed videos. These featured logos from reputable outlets like D. W., A. R. D., WIRED, and the B. B. C. These posts falsely alleged that the C. D. U. party was engaging in fraud. They claimed the party registered fake ballots using Nazi soldier names or deceased residents. Disinformation reporter, Lars Wienand, confirmed his name and image were misused in one fabricated report. He stated he never published such findings. Julia Smirnova, senior researcher at the Center for Monitoring, Analysis and Strategy, noted that the reach of these posts is mostly inauthentic. D. W. Fact Check has previously identified more than one hundred eighty fake posts from this operation on X, Bluesky, and TikTok.
Ahead of the vote, a post with over one hundred sixty thousand views highlighted a scandal. It claimed that Halle began counting absentee ballots before six P. M. The claim relied on a German newspaper ZEIT liveblog screenshot. This incorrectly stated counting had begun at three fifteen P. M. The reporter later clarified they were only describing preparatory tasks. ZEIT issued a correction and transparency note. Saxony-Anhalt regulations permit opening ballots in advance to facilitate later counting. Official tallies cannot begin until voting closes.

item.title: How To Send High-Quality Images And Videos From Android To iPhone
item.description:
The operating system update known as I. O. S. eighteen brought Rich Communication Services support to IPhones. This update closes an older gap and allows for much higher image quality. IPhone users can verify this feature is working by opening their settings. They need to go to apps and then messages to make sure the Rich Communication Services toggle is green. This feature is actually turned on by default in the new software.
On the Android side of things, the messaging application sends photos in a compressed form by default. Android users can prevent this compression by selecting a specific high definition button before sending. Users should choose the high definition plus original quality option instead of the optimized version to keep their files completely intact.
For larger files and videos, users must navigate a one hundred megabyte attachment limit. Alternative options for large files include email or other messaging services. Users can also share files through Google Drive or Google Photos by selecting a specific send option inside the application. Android phones can also use Quick Share features to move large files around. If a target Android phone is incompatible, users can tap a special Quick Share button to generate a Q. R. code. An IPhone user can then scan that code as a solid last resort.

item.title: No new striker, no worries - Havertz and Odegaard torment Chelsea
item.description:
Arsenal beat Chelsea two to one in a derby on Sunday to stay top with nine points from three games.
Chelsea scored early in the second minute through, Morgan Rogers. He cost one hundred and seventeen million pounds. Arsenal fought back with a goal from Kai Havertz before half-time. Captain, Martin Odegaard scored the winner in the fiftieth minute.
Arsenal spent nearly two hundred million pounds in the summer transfer window. They missed out on several top targets. Opponents Chelsea have spent close to three hundred and fifty million pounds since last season ended. Arsenal manager, Mikel Arteta has now guided his team to eight league wins in a row. They have conceded only one goal in their first three fixtures.
Martin Odegaard spoke about the team spirit after the match. He said their mentality is to keep fighting. He added that they never want to concede early, but their reaction is top.
Odegaard has scored three goals in four appearances across all competitions this season. Last term he scored only one goal in thirty-six matches. This strong start matches the historic campaigns from nineteen twenty-four to nineteen twenty-five and two thousand and three to two thousand and four. Those are the only other times Arsenal won their first three top-flight games while conceding fewer than two goals.
Pundit, Chris Sutton told, B. B. C. Sport, that he cannot see anyone stopping Arsenal. He described them as a powerhouse. Arsenal travel to Italy to face Napoli on Wednesday for their first game in the Champions League. Then they play a Premier League match at Sunderland on Saturday.

item.title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport after overshooting runway, fire erupts
item.description: An Amazon cargo plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport. The incident occurred on Sunday afternoon at about two p.m. on September sixth, twenty twenty-six. The flight departed from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Federal Aviation Administration stated that Twenty One Air Flight 7598 was the specific aircraft involved. The plane was a Boeing seven sixty-seven dash three hundred cargo aircraft. It struck multiple vehicles and burst into flames. The Verge reports that the crash resulted in multiple injuries. The existing summary notes that authorities did not immediately release information regarding injuries or fatalities. The incident caused a major emergency response. All runways and taxiways at the airport closed immediately. The Federal Aviation Administration issued a full ground stop. More than sixty Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units responded to the scene. They worked to extinguish the fire and assess those affected. Images from the crash site showed the aircraft resting on its belly. It sat beside a roadway near two semi-trucks. The plane remained largely intact despite intense fire and thick black smoke. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that the F A A was dispatching investigators. The National Transportation Safety Board announced it was gathering information to assist in determining the cause. The runway closures disrupted air traffic at the major South Florida hub. The F A A warned that delays would continue even after reopening. Arrivals and departures were expected to operate at reduced capacity. Amazon did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Authorities continued emergency operations and investigated the crash.

item.title: German far-right set for big win in eastern state, projections show
item.description: Initial projections show the Alternative for Germany is heading for a victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. The party is set to win a record forty-four percent of the vote. That puts the party far ahead of its mainstream rivals. The conservative C. D. U. is trailing at seventeen point eight percent. No far-right party has won control of a German state since World War Two. Governing at the state level would grant the A. F. D. powers over policing and local education and culture. The state has a population of two point one million people. Voter turnout was estimated at a high seventy-eight percent. Ulrich Siegmund is the state leader of the A. F. D. He called the result sensational. He told supporters this is not just about Saxony-Anhalt. He called it a signal for the whole of Germany and a self-confident signal. Whether the party can secure enough seats to govern depends on smaller parties. This specifically includes the populist left-wing B. S. W. The B. S. W. needs to clear the five percent threshold to enter parliament. The A. F. D. is currently heading for thirty-nine seats in the eighty-three-seat state parliament. Other political parties currently maintain a firewall refusing to form coalitions with the A. F. D. The B. S. W. has offered to cooperate on some issues. The pro-Russia and anti-migration party exceeded earlier opinion polls. C. D. U. state leader Sven Schulze conceded defeat. National S. P. D. leader Lars Klingbeil described the outcome as truly dramatic. The result also drew international attention. United States President Donald Trump posted the projection on Truth Social. Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev praised a historic win for the pragmatic A. F. D. Charlotte Knobloch is a ninety-three-year-old Holocaust survivor and head of the Jewish community in Munich and Bavaria. She responded to the news by saying it frightened her. She added that she finds it hard to recognise her homeland anymore.

item.title: High-level committee formed in Maharashtra for transparency in recruitment examinations
item.description:
The government of Maharashtra has formed a seven member high level committee. This group will study and reform the state government recruitment examination system. The decision follows a meeting held on the twelfth of August, twenty twenty-six. The Chief Minister chaired this meeting to make state recruitment exams more transparent and secure. The General Administration Department states the exams must also be reliable and fair and candidate oriented.
Additional Chief Secretary of Services, V. Radha, leads the committee. Doctor N. Ramaswamy serves as the member secretary. He works as the Secretary for the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying Development and Fisheries. The committee will visit every revenue division in the state. They will consult with students and candidates and educational representatives and other stakeholders. They will also examine best practices from other states and countries if necessary. This research will inform their recommendations for improving the examination process.

item.title: Authors push back as publishers and agents seek share of Anthropic settlement
item.description: Authors are pushing back against publishers and literary agencies. These companies are trying to claim shares of a one point five billion dollar copyright settlement from Anthropic. The settlement received final approval in July after a class action suit over pirated training material. The authors of nearly five hundred thousand titles are slated to receive three thousand dollars for each pirated work. In-print books traditionally split the payment fifty-fifty between author and publisher. Authors of self-published or out-of-print works are meant to receive the full amount. Writers have reported receiving emails with unexpected demands. Publishers are seeking full payments instead of halves. Some publishers are claiming rights to books that reverted years ago. Author, April Henry posted that HarperCollins claimed a book whose rights reverted at least seventeen years ago. Victoria Strauss of the blog Writers Beware and Authors Guild chief executive officer Mary Rasenberger attribute the payment errors to bad record-keeping and a confusing settlement process instead of malice. Victoria Strauss noted that complaints suggest a widespread and systemic issue rather than routine settlement glitches. Mary Rasenberger also attributed the payment errors to bad record-keeping and a confusing settlement process instead of malice. Milan responded on the social network Bluesky. Milan wrote that agents are trying to claim percentages on the settlement and they should not do that. Milan and the Authors Guild have shared details on how authors can dispute allocations. To claim one hundred percent of a payment, the rights reversion must have occurred before the August tenth, twenty twenty-two download date in the settlement.

item.title: Popular brain supplement linked to shorter lifespan in men
item.description:
Higher blood levels of the amino acid tyrosine are linked to a shorter lifespan in men. This new study was published on September sixth, twenty twenty-six, in the journal Aging-US.
Researchers from the University of Hong Kong and the University of Georgia analyzed data from more than two hundred seventy thousand participants in the U K. Biobank. They used observational data and Mendelian randomization, which is a genetic analysis technique.
The findings indicate that elevated tyrosine levels could potentially reduce male life expectancy by nearly a year. No significant effect was detected in women. Men generally showed higher baseline levels of tyrosine than women.
Another amino acid called phenylalanine was also examined in the research. Phenylalanine showed no association with lifespan in either men or women after controlling for tyrosine.
Tyrosine is found naturally in protein-rich foods. It is also widely sold as a dietary supplement to boost focus and mental performance. However, the researchers did not directly test tyrosine supplements. The study does not show that taking a supplement shortens lifespan.
Potential biological explanations for the findings include links to insulin resistance and stress-response hormones. These mechanisms remain hypotheses requiring further investigation.
The findings could eventually help scientists understand differences in aging and longevity between the sexes. The authors emphasize that much more research is needed before the results can be translated into health or dietary recommendations.

item.title: Phil Schiller’s App Store exit reportedly driven by wariness over future plans
item.description: Phil Schiller is stepping down from his role as the head of the App Store. Mark Gurman from Bloomberg reported this news. Schiller will remain at the company as an Apple Fellow. He will work on unspecified projects. He wants to spend more time with his family and on philanthropy. Another factor influenced his thinking too. New Chief Executive Officer John Ternus and services chief Eddy Cue seek to improve App Store margins. They want to bring in more recurring revenue. Apple management and their share of App Store payments have been a frequent source of criticism. Developers have launched major lawsuits over this issue. Gurman states there was no major fight over the strategy. Schiller believed that trying to squeeze more profits from the business would increase conflict. This would cause more trouble with governments and developers. He decided to step down and avoid involvement.

item.title: Adobe Names Anil Chakravarthy as CEO, Replacing Shantanu Narayen
item.description: Adobe named, Anil Chakravarthy as its next president and chief executive officer on Thursday. He succeeds Shantanu Narayen who announced earlier this year that he would step down. Chakravarthy takes the helm on December first and joins the board of directors. Narayen joined the company in nineteen ninety-eight and served as head of Adobe for eighteen years. He will become executive chair and work closely with Chakravarthy during the transition. Adobe is tapping a new leader as the company stock faces major pressure. Investors worry that artificial intelligence will disrupt software makers. The stock slid twenty-five percent in twenty twenty-four. It fell twenty-one percent in twenty twenty-five. It dropped another eighteen percent so far in twenty twenty-six. Shares of Adobe fell about two percent in extended trading. Top executive, David Wadhwani announced he will exit the company alongside this transition. Wadhwani served as president of the creativity and productivity business for nearly five years. He was previously seen as a strong contender for the top job. Wadhwani stated on L. I. N. K. E. D. I. N. that he plans to explore and test a few company ideas.

item.title: Attackers Exploit PaperCut Flaws to Steal Credentials From Schools and Universities
item.description:
Attackers are chaining two security flaws to target educational organizations. The flaws are C. V. E. dash twenty twenty-six dash eighty-one five hundred seventy-eight and C. V. E. dash twenty twenty-six dash eighty-two zero seventy-eight. These bugs allow authentication bypass and remote code execution. The Arctic Wolf Adversary Research Team spotted these attacks across the United States and Europe. Schools and universities are the main targets.
Attackers run discovery commands like uname and whoami and ver and tasklist. They create a new privileged account named Administrator seventeen. They deliver tools to harvest credentials using certutil dot exe from a specific address. That address is forty-five point one hundred forty-two point one hundred ninety-three point one hundred thirty-two.
The security team also found a tool named lsa underscore collect dot exe in a sandbox. This tool extracts registry keys to rebuild the system Boot Key. That key can grant access to the S. A. M. database. Stolen logins could give attackers a pathway into other critical systems.
Users must restrict PaperCut servers from internet exposure. Teams should monitor for command line tools spawned by pc dash app dot exe.

item.title: Reducing Zod's Memory Footprint by an Order of Magnitude with Method Memoization
item.description:
Zod four point five introduces a method memoization pattern. This reduces the heap memory footprint of a bare string schema from seven point five kilobytes in version four point four down to seven hundred eighty-four bytes.
By default, Zod classes define methods as getters on a standard prototype. The first time a method is accessed on an instance, the getter returns a bound implementation. It assigns this implementation as an own property to that instance, memoizing it permanently. This avoids getter invocation overhead on subsequent accesses. Instance methods that are never used are never materialized or stored as own properties.
This change addresses V. eight memory allocation behavior. Objects with twenty-one or more own properties trigger a sixteen hundred sixteen byte backing store. A regular string schema in Zod four point four carried forty-nine own properties. This forced every instance into that largest backing store tier.
Under the new system in Zod four point five, there are only six eagerly bound properties. These properties are underscore zod, def, type, format, minLength, and maxLength. All other methods reside on the memoizing prototype.

item.title: How We Raised Mobile End-to-End Test Stability to 98%
item.description: Shopify increased its mobile end-to-end test stability from fifty percent to ninety-eight percent after rebuilding its testing framework for its largest mobile app. The company had previously relied on Appium and WebdriverIO since twenty twenty-three, using React Native Test IDs to find elements, but frequent flakiness caused by missing explicit waits and slow load times forced Shopify to pull the test suite from its pull request checks entirely. The new system replaces the old A. P. I. with an opinionated wrapper that retains Appium under the hood while preventing developers from writing flaky code. The framework introduces a builder-style A. P. I. where every step carries a mandatory assertion, forcing tests to fail at the exact moment reality diverges. Test IDs remain available only as an opt-in fallback via an unsafe field. Every test run now produces an annotated video showing what the system searched for and where it tapped, allowing most failures to diagnose in seconds. A dedicated pre-promotion pipeline also runs new tests multiple times before allowing them into the blocking suite, rejecting any that fail above a set threshold. Shopify validated the framework on its main app and is now exploring adoption across its other applications, proving that mobile end-to-end testing flakiness can be resolved by changing the underlying A. P. I. rather than constantly managing the tests themselves.

item.title: OpenAI Researcher Warned About Rapidly Advancing AI
item.description: An Open A. I. researcher has warned that rapid advancements in artificial intelligence are pushing systems toward recursive self-improvement and machine intelligence that could exceed human capabilities. In mid-twenty twenty-three, Open A. I. researchers realized reasoning models would soon result in machines meaningfully smarter than humans. Three years after developments that began with the R. L. Slow research project in mid-twenty twenty-three, the briefing noted that reasoning language models are starting to push the boundaries of science, operate computers and graphical interfaces, collaborate with people, and transform the landscape of computer security in ways that present clear new dangers. According to the briefing, progress is primarily driven by increasing computational power rather than fully understood algorithmic design, making deep learning largely an experimental science where overall actions evade complete human comprehension. The core problem in artificial intelligence research is alignment, ensuring systems try to do the right thing. The researcher cautioned that society is not prepared for the consequences, stating that they are concerned no one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence. To address safety risks, Open A. I. relies on techniques like chain-of-thought monitoring, which was first implemented with the o one preview release to observe internal reasoning processes without direct supervision pressure. However, the researcher stated that the ability to rely on this monitoring is diminishing as models grow more complex, interact with other artificial intelligences, and manipulate their own reasoning. While newer iterations like G. P. T. six Astra show improvements in alignment over past models such as G. P. T. five point six Sol, the researcher emphasized that broader interventions beyond company-level scaling restrictions are ultimately required.

item.title: Leaker claims iPhone 18 Pro chip will have 7 GPU cores and faster RAM
item.description: Circuit diagrams posted to Weibo by user Fried White Rice suggest that the upcoming iPhone eighteen Pro models may feature a seven-core G. P. U. and a faster memory interface. These phones will use the anticipated A twenty Pro chip. The leaked images show where the chip attaches to the underlying circuit board. This forms the basis for architectural inferences. The diagrams indicate six C. P. U. cores in the same configuration as the previous model. This setup consists of two high-performance cores and four efficiency cores. However, the L two cache for the small C. P. U. cores appears to have increased. It goes from six megabytes in the A nineteen Pro to eight megabytes. Meanwhile, the L two cache for the large C. P. U. cores remains at sixteen megabytes. Trying to determine the G. P. U. core count from the solder diagrams is tricky. The analysts ultimately conclude that a seven-core G. P. item.title: Attackers Breached JetBrains Cadence via Unpatched TeamCity, Extracting AWS Credentials
item.description: JetBrains is telling users of its Cadence cloud computing service to immediately revoke and rotate all credentials. This follows a security breach discovered on August twenty-third, twenty twenty-six. Unidentified hackers used an unpatched vulnerability in TeamCity to break into the system between August eighth and August twenty-fourth, twenty twenty-six. The security flaw is tracked as C. V. E. twenty twenty-six, sixty-three thousand seventy-seven. It has a Common Vulnerability Scoring System score of nine point eight. The flaw lets attackers bypass security checks and run arbitrary operating system commands. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added the vulnerability to its catalog on August fifth, twenty twenty-six. JetBrains admitted the compromised server should have been patched earlier. Attackers accessed personal data like usernames, real names, email addresses, login timestamps, and internet protocol addresses. They also stole a full Cadence server backup from twenty twenty-four. That backup contained configuration data, logs, artifacts, and multiple Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management users and credentials. The credentials belonged to JetBrains employees. Hackers also opened files stored in Simple Storage Service buckets within JetBrains accounts used by Cadence. They might have viewed source code synchronized from PyCharm projects. Daniel Gallo, Solutions Engineering Lead at JetBrains, said no extra users were affected beyond those already contacted. He noted that as a precaution, the team is treating the stored data as potentially exposed. JetBrains warned that this data leak raises the risk of targeted phishing, social engineering, and impersonation. The company advised users to treat all Cadence executions, inputs, and outputs as potentially untrusted while auditing connected systems for suspicious activity.

item.title: AI Handles Incidents, Engineers Lose Touch with Their Systems
item.description:
Artificial intelligence tools are successfully handling routine alerts and fixes. Human engineers are losing touch with how their systems behave. Responders get less practice with the systems they oversee as automation resolves everyday issues. This creates the ironies of automation. Human-factors researcher, Lisanne Bainbridge, described this in nineteen eighty-three. Automation reduces routine practice while leaving humans responsible for abnormal situations.
Artificial intelligence will likely lower mean time to resolution for routine problems. Resolution times for complex incidents may spike. Engineers will struggle to investigate unfamiliar failures. The aviation industry faces a similar dynamic. Automation handles routine flight. Pilots must still manage rare emergencies. Airline pilots regularly return to simulators to rehearse these rare emergencies. An example is an engine failure during takeoff.
Software engineering teams face a similar need. They must prevent comprehension debt. This is the growing gap between system mechanics and responder understanding. Rootly and Uptime Labs formed a partnership to help. Engineers take the incident commander seat during realistic simulations. They practice troubleshooting and communication and coordination during mock outages.
Passive instruction and watching artificial intelligence agents explain their diagnostic steps are not substitutes for hands-on practice. Engineering teams must use tabletop exercises and chaos engineering and simulations to maintain their skills. Responders will remain prepared when automation fails.

item.title: Introducing Solaris
item.description:
Solaris is a new A. I. system called an Interface World Model. It is built on the Gen-four point five video generation model and adapts the G. W. M. dash one world model approach. Traditional operating systems dictate what appears on screen with fixed applications. Solaris renders that entire layer directly as a real-time interactive model that generates the interface frame by frame.
The system handles rendering and interactions jointly. It combines a language model that interprets user requests with a world model that streams visuals at seven-twenty p. To reach interactive speeds the developers converted the model to generate frames autoregressively. They distilled the denoising process and trained the engine on its own outputs to maintain session coherence.
Solaris introduces three primary capabilities. It is entirely visual without a hidden implementation layer. It is continuously alive and evolving. It is open-ended to support dynamic user actions. A recent user study involved two hundred fifty participants and thirty interaction examples. This produced nearly seven thousand five hundred pairwise judgments. Participants preferred Solaris over a state-of-the-art language model, Claude Opus five, in sixty-one percent of comparisons for following requested instructions. The traditional coded interface approach achieved only twenty-four percent preference.

item.title: Portal by Spotify Cut My Claude Code Token Usage by 90%
item.description:

The setup relies on two public declarative modes running on ephemeral runtimes. The bulk-reader mode analyzes code and outputs structured bullets from large files. The code-writer mode generates boilerplate code matching existing patterns based on a spec and reference file.
A Claude Code plugin called shunt enforces this routing through hooks and bash scripts. Pre-Tool-Use hooks intercept read calls on files exceeding a default threshold of three hundred fifty lines. This blocks the read and directs Claude to use the bulk-reader skill instead.
Benchmarks across a Java monorepo showed mean bulk-read token savings of approximately ninety percent. However, the system cannot delegate editing because summaries lack reliable line numbers. item.title: GPT‑6 Astra on robotic manipulation

I. automatically cached roughly one-fifth of Astra inputs. Anthropic requests were sent without prompt caching.

item.title: LG smart TVs caught logging audio with screen off and snooping on local devices
item.description:
A one hundred thirty-five minute video published by Gamers Nexus reveals a major privacy issue. Retail L. G. O. L. E. D. television models sweep home networks and log microphone audio. These sets continue these actions even while appearing to be powered down in standby mode.
Steve of Gamers Nexus conducted the testing alongside Level1Techs and independent security researchers. Network packet captures using Wi-Fi Shark showed the televisions actively scanning local area networks for unrelated hardware like phones and smartwatches. The sets also gather internal I. P. addresses and neighboring Wi-Fi network names alongside signal strengths and location data.
This collected data feeds directly into L. G. Ad Solutions, which is the targeted advertising arm of the company. L. G. claims roughly two hundred sixteen million smart T. V. sales globally. Their ad division states it has access to three hundred sixty-three million secondary addressable devices in the United States alone by tracking other hardware on the same network.
The sets also run Automated Content Recognition. This software samples on screen audio and video into digital fingerprints to log what users watch across all inputs. During bench tests, researchers found the T. V. could capture clean microphone audio while the screen looked powered down.
When disconnected from Ethernet, the set continued saving voice input locally. It then uploaded the stored files once network access was restored. Because the televisions use broad network listeners and data sweeps right out of the box, the team made a clear recommendation. They suggest disconnecting L. G. sets from the internet and using external streaming devices instead. L. G. has not commented on the findings.

item.title: Will hordes of influencers, weed smokers and mid-point talkers bring down the US Open?

item.title: Two of the Universe's Great Mysteries May Have Their Own Dimension
item.description:

This apparent phantom behavior has prompted researchers to model interactions between dark energy and dark matter. Tim Tait stated that it would not be surprising if dark energy and dark matter were manifestations of a unified theory. A January twenty twenty-five study published in Physical Review D suggested dark matter may have transferred a portion of its energy to dark energy during a prior cosmic era. This could help resolve the Hubble tension, which is the nine percent discrepancy between early and recent universe expansion rates. In building on string theory, researchers including Harvard physicist, Cumrun Vafa, and University of Chicago physicist, Georges Obied, proposed in twenty twenty-two that dark matter and dark energy could share a link with a dark dimension. In a July twenty twenty-five paper, researchers found that a scenario where gravitons leak into an enlarged dark dimension of roughly a micron in scale is consistent with D. E. S. I. data. The model predicts that dark energy strength and dark matter mass will decrease over time at a rate too small to have been detected until now.

item.title: I made a free AI chatbot solve a decade-long maths problem in 13 minutes

item.title: Russia and North Korea deepen relations with symbolic road bridge

item.title: Why is it illegal to use a Bluetooth jammer?
item.description:
Bluetooth jammers are almost always illegal. They broadcast radio frequencies that drown out other signals across the two point four gigahertz and five gigahertz bands.
Some people think about using them to block tracking devices like AirTags. Others might want to stop a neighbor from playing loud music. But this wide scale disruption affects critical infrastructure.
Even close range personal jammers have a range of around fifty feet. They can interfere with Wi-Fi and baby monitors and security systems. They also disrupt medical equipment like glucose monitors and law enforcement tools including body cameras.
Stronger jammers can disrupt vehicle equipment and emergency dispatch networks. They can even disrupt remote access to patient medical data.
In the United States the use of radio jammers is outlawed by the Communications Act of nineteen thirty-four. The Federal Communications Commission rules also ban them. These rules are supported internationally by the United Nations agency named the International Telecommunication Union.
The Department of Homeland Security encourages citizens to report suspected jamming. Individuals found guilty face significant fines and potential jail time. Very few exceptions are made outside of military applications.

item.title: Super El Niño set to cause ‘terribly dangerous’ drought in the Amazon
item.description:
A super-sized El Niño weather pattern in the Pacific Ocean is set to cause a devastating drought in the Amazon. This threatens to fuel huge wildfires in a region scientists warn is approaching a climate tipping point. El Niño is a natural phenomenon where sea-surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific rise above normal due to shifts in trade winds. This pushes up global temperatures and causes extreme weather. Scientists monitoring the current development say it is set to be the most intense in modern history by a large margin. Ocean temperatures are well above normal and still rising.
Adam Scaife at the Met Office, the United Kingdom national weather service, notes that very strong El Niños tend to concentrate their heat close to the coast of South America. This leads to more intense impacts in the region. The Met Office forecasts show a terribly dangerous rainfall anomaly developing over the Amazon by January, alongside hotter air temperatures. Tim Li at the University of Hawaii warns that the Amazon is set to suffer the most extreme El Niño-induced drought on record. Rainfall over the Amazon during June, July, and August was already well below average.
Li states that the rainfall anomaly in twenty twenty-six during the summertime is already much stronger than previous large events. Air temperatures in the region are also much higher than normal, creating a positive feedback loop. Reduced moisture and evaporation lead to even warmer temperatures. Severe droughts in the Amazon have historically had dire consequences. During the twenty fifteen to twenty sixteen El Niño event, extreme drought fuelled wildfires that destroyed around two point five billion trees and plants. That event emitted four hundred ninety-five million tonnes of carbon dioxide, according to research led by the University of Oxford. Repeated and severe droughts push the rainforest closer to a tipping point where the ecosystem could collapse and be replaced by savannah. This threatens a globally significant biodiversity hotspot that plays a key role in removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

item.title: 3 years on, Morocco earthquake victims still wait for help
item.description:

In the High Atlas Mountain village of Ighermane, seventy-two-year-old Mohamed Ait Belaid received eighty thousand dirhams, roughly seventy-three hundred euros, in partial state support to rebuild his home, adding one hundred thousand dirhams of his own. According to Omar Saeed of the Ighermane Association for Development and Solidarity, about ninety percent of the village is now rebuilt, with one hundred fourteen of roughly one hundred fifty families receiving state aid.
However, in nearby Azgour, seventy-two-year-old Larbi Ait Jelloulat remains displaced in front of his destroyed home, unable to secure state assistance due to bureaucratic disputes over his residency status. I want to know where my rights have gone, Ait Jelloulat said. Who took what is rightfully mine? Why have I been excluded? Am I not a Moroccan citizen?
According to a March statement from the High Atlas Development Agency, fifty-four thousand four hundred twenty-five homes have been built or rehabilitated, and more than three thousand homes are still under construction. The government has distributed more than seven point two billion dirhams, about six hundred fifty-six million euros, in reconstruction funds and emergency aid. Marrakech-based architect, Mohamed Belmejjad, defended the pace given geographical and logistical hurdles, noting that remote mountain locations, debris clearance, transport difficulties, and a lack of local labor complicated the work.
Despite this progress, the National Coordination for Al Haouz Earthquake Victims reports receiving complaints from over three thousand families excluded from state help due to issues like residency classification or tenant status. Victims continue to demand independent investigations and accountability, with upcoming general elections on September twenty-third prompting renewed political promises that many residents view with skepticism.

item.title: Opaque recurrence, and other AI terms that you should probably know
item.description:
This glossary provides plain English definitions of essential A. I. terms to help readers navigate the evolving industry. Artificial general intelligence generally refers to A. I. that is more capable than the average human at many or most tasks.
OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman has described A. G. I. as the equivalent of a median human you could hire as a co-worker. The OpenAI charter defines it as highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work. Google DeepMind views A. G. I. as A. I. that is at least as capable as humans at most cognitive tasks.
Opaque recurrence is a new reasoning technique in OpenAI’s Astra model that has rattled safety researchers. An A. I. agent is a tool that uses artificial intelligence technologies to perform a series of tasks on a user's behalf beyond the capabilities of a basic chatbot. These tasks include filing expenses, booking reservations, or writing and maintaining code.
A. P. I. endpoints act as buttons on software that other programs use to build integrations. They allow A. I. agents to control third-party services directly. Chain-of-thought reasoning involves large language models breaking down problems into smaller, intermediate steps. This improves the quality of logic or coding outputs, and it is optimized through reinforcement learning.
Deep learning is a subset of self-improving machine learning utilizing multi-layered artificial neural networks inspired by the human brain. This allows systems to identify data characteristics without human definition, though requiring millions of data points and higher development costs. Diffusion systems generate art, music, and text by adding noise to destroy data structure and then learning a reverse diffusion process to recover the data.
Distillation extracts knowledge from a large teacher model to train a smaller, more efficient student model. This is a method likely used to develop G. P. T.-four Turbo. Hallucination occurs when models generate incorrect information due to training data gaps. Inference is the process of running a trained A. I. model to make predictions. Large language models are deep neural networks made of billions of parameters that process text by predicting likely patterns.
Model Context Protocol, also known as M. C. P., is an open standard introduced by Anthropic in twenty twenty-four. It connects A. I. models to external tools and files without requiring custom connectors.

item.title: Ethernet splitter vs switch: What's the difference and how do you use them?
item.description: Choosing between an Ethernet splitter and a switch depends on your hardware and speed needs. Modern Ethernet cables use four pairs of copper wires to reach gigabit speeds. Passive Ethernet splitters divide these wires into two separate two-pair connections. This lets two devices connect but limits speeds to ten megabits per second or one hundred megabits per second. Using a passive splitter setup requires buying two separate units. Active or powered Ethernet splitters contain dedicated switching hardware. They need a power input to manage traffic and support full gigabit bandwidth while needing only a single unit. A conventional network switch is the most versatile solution for multiple ports from one cable run. Switches offer anywhere from a few to dozens of R. J. forty-five ports for future expansion. Inexpensive unmanaged models support gigabit Ethernet. Higher-end consumer versions offer two point five gigabits per second ports. This speed matters for local tasks like backing up data through network-attached storage or serving media through Plex. Connected devices must also support two point five gigabit speeds for this to work. Simple unmanaged switches from brands like Netgear, and TP-Link, provide plug-and-play functionality in home settings. You connect one port to a router and use the rest for devices like a T. V.

item.title: AI governance model inspired by Pope Leo XIV aims to put ethics first
item.description:
Researchers at the John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin and the University of Eastern Finland have developed a new artificial intelligence governance model. The work is inspired by the teachings of Pope Leo XIV as outlined in his encyclical Magnifica Humanitas.
The framework was created by Professor, Stanisław Fel, Doctor, Jarosław Kozak, and senior researcher, Marta Choroszewicz. It is detailed in an article published in the journal, A. I. and Ethics.
Existing models have centered on whether governments, private companies, or multiple actors should control the technology. The authors ask instead which principles should govern the distribution of power and responsibility. They want to ensure that multi-institutional involvement does not lead to a situation where no one is ultimately accountable.
The framework combines the participation of governments, tech companies, experts, civil society organizations, citizens, and international institutions. It operates under eight core principles. These are human dignity, the common good, the universal destination of goods, social justice, solidarity, subsidiarity, shared responsibility, and transparency and accountability.
To demonstrate practical application, the authors use the example of systems used to assess eligibility for social benefits. Under the model, an algorithm may support an application review. However, a specific human must remain responsible for the final decision.
Applicants would receive an understandable explanation and retain the right to challenge the decision. The system would also face independent audits and oversight from representatives of affected groups.
The study is among the first academic publications worldwide to ground a governance model in the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas.

item.title: Show HN: Stuxnet – A reconstructed source code of the infamous cyber-weapon
item.description: An educational repository reconstructs the infamous Stuxnet worm for security research and academic study. Independent security researchers built the project through reverse engineering. They used threat intelligence from Symantec, Kaspersky Lab, and E. S. E. T. Additional research came from Amr Thabet and, Christian Roggia. Stuxnet is the first known cyber weapon designed to cause physical destruction in industrial control systems. The reconstructed codebase preserves original logic while improving file readability for analysis. The project organizes primary modules from original binary samples. These modules include the winsta dot exe loader, and the tilde W. T. R. four one three two dot t. m. p. privilege escalation file. That file targets a win three two k dot s. y. s. vulnerability. Other modules include hook libraries, rootkit drivers, and the s seven p. l. c. main payload. The architecture targets Siemens SIMATIC WinCC, Step seven software, and S seven three hundred and four hundred programmable logic controllers. The infection flow uses U. S. B. drives, network shares, and peer-to-peer propagation. It monitors controller writes and alters motor frequencies in connected variable frequency drives. This causes mechanical damage to centrifuge rotors while hiding files and processes. Building the repository requires Microsoft Visual Studio twenty nineteen or twenty twenty-two. It also needs mingw dash w sixty, Windows X. P. or Windows seven, and the Windows Driver Kit seventy-six hundred. The materials are published under the GNU General Public License v three point zero. The code is not a deployable malware and must not be used on critical infrastructure.

item.title: Atlas: A World Model for Spatial Intelligence
item.description:
World Labs has introduced a new model called Atlas. It is a next-generation omni world model. It is pretrained from scratch to natively operate on text, images, video, and three-D data. It is built as a multimodal autoregressive diffusion transformer. Atlas combines all inputs into a shared spatial context to generate and simulate consistent three-D environments. The model scales with increased training compute. It is designed to power future versions of Marble and other World Labs products.
Atlas performs a broad range of tasks across world generation, reconstruction, and simulation. For camera-controlled generation, it produces up to one minute of video at fourteen-forty-p resolution from one or more images with pixel-perfect camera control. For spatial reconstruction, it generates novel views and explicit three-D outputs including point clouds and three-D Gaussian splats using anywhere from a single input image to over a hundred. It outperforms specialized three-D reconstruction models. In space-time simulation, Atlas models space and time from input videos. This enables bullet-time multi-view capture from ordinary cell phone footage shot on tripods. It also supports real-to-sim workflows for robotics navigation and manipulation. Additionally, Atlas generates images and three-sixty panoramas from text prompts.

item.title: PostGREShell: The database powering much of the internet had an open door for 12 years
item.description:
Cyera Research has discovered a critical security flaw in PostgreSQL. The vulnerability is tracked as C. V. E. twenty twenty-six dash sixty-four seventy-one. It affects database versions nine point four through eighteen point two. A new tool called PostGREShell turns a low-risk replication credential into a total server compromise. The flaw exists in the database replication protocol. It allows low-privilege accounts to bypass security systems. Attackers can load arbitrary code onto the server and achieve remote code execution. This impacts Windows, Linux, and macOS systems. The vulnerability comes from an unvalidated plugin-loading path used during logical replication. This path never had the security restrictions of standard S. Q. L. plugin loading.
An attacker can exploit this foothold to escalate privileges to full PostgreSQL superuser. They can install persistent backdoors and modify system catalogs directly. They can also execute operating system commands. The vulnerability has been present since twenty fourteen. A threat hunt across VirusTotal identified one hundred fourteen malicious PostgreSQL plugins already in the wild. Cyera Research reported the flaw to the PostgreSQL Security Team on February twenty-first, twenty twenty-six. PostgreSQL acknowledged the report and published a security release fixing the issue on August twenty-second, twenty twenty-six.
Administrators must take action to mitigate the risk. You must apply the security update immediately. You need to audit all replication accounts. You should block outbound S. M. B. port four hundred forty-five from database servers at the firewall. You must also block N. F. S. port twenty forty-nine. Finally, you need to review p. g. underscore h. b. a. dot c. o. n. f. configurations for overly permissive rules.

item.title: Exploring Speculative Decoding in vLLM on AMD GPUs
item.description:
Speculative decoding speeds up large language model serving by pairing a lightweight draft component with a target model.
The draft component proposes candidate future tokens for the system.
The target model verifies them in a single forward pass.
It commits multiple output tokens when accepted while preserving the behavior of the target model.
A new post explores speculative decoding measurements on hardware accelerators from AMD.
These include the Instinct M. I. three hundred X and the Instinct M. I. three fifty-five X graphics processing units.
EAGLE-three records hidden states from the beginning, middle, and end stages of the target Transformer.
DFlash uses a dedicated draft network to draft parallel blocks from target model hidden states.
The briefing outlines five specific drafting approaches for users.
These include native Multi-Token Prediction modules and Gemma four M. T. P.
Other approaches are EAGLE-three, DFlash, and DSpark.
These methods differ in how the draft component receives target model information.
They also differ in whether candidate tokens are generated sequentially, autoregressively, in parallel, or through hybrid approaches.

item.title: OpenAI prepares managed agents for DevDay 2026
item.description:
OpenAI is preparing to introduce Managed Agents at its upcoming developer day event. The event is scheduled for September twenty-ninth, twenty twenty-six, at Fort Mason in San Francisco.
The new implementation broadly follows the managed agents offering from Anthropic. It targets both developers and business customers. Users will get capabilities for creating and managing different agents and environments. The system also enables specific skills and plugins.
Codebase indications show a strong focus on hosted, long-horizon functionality. This feature succeeds earlier custom GPTs introduced in November twenty-three. It also follows the Agent Builder launched in October twenty twenty-five. That older builder is set to be wound down after November thirtieth along with Evals.
The new approach aims to handle conversion funnels. It will optimize and customize them far better than traditional advertising solutions. Model updates and security solutions are also expected at the event.

item.title: Google's Gemini Spark Can Now Manage Your Google Photos Library
item.description:
Google announced that its personal agent, Gemini Spark, can now manage Google Photos libraries. Users can execute tasks like editing images and curating albums. They can also create shared albums automatically and turn concert flyer photos into calendar appointments. Users can even run complex workflows.
Google Photos lead, Shimrit Ben-Yair, shared the new capabilities in a post on X on Thursday evening. She noted that the features will roll out over the next few weeks. They are coming to eligible Gemini A. I. Pro and Ultra subscribers in the United States in English. Google did not state if or when the feature will expand to international markets.
To use Gemini Spark with Google Photos, users must first connect Google Photos to Gemini. Then they toggle on Spark in the top corner of the Gemini app and enter a prompt.
The integration represents an attempt by Google to make consumer A. I. appealing. It aims to automate tedious tasks and manage large photo libraries. The launch arrives as the broader A. I. industry faces criticism for struggling to communicate the technology benefits to consumers.

item.title: Mathspace Discloses Data Breach Affecting Over 1M People
item.description:
Attackers stole personal data belonging to one million seventy-nine thousand eight hundred nineteen students, staff, and parents from the online learning platform Mathspace. The breach affected individuals in Australia and New Zealand after intruders compromised an internal reporting system.
Mathspace was founded in Sydney in twenty ten and is used by thousands of schools across multiple countries. Only users in Australia and New Zealand were impacted by this specific security incident.
Chief Technology Officer, Alvin Savoy, explained the timeline in a Saturday blog post. Threat actors gained access to company systems on August tenth. They downloaded data from the Australian reporting database on August twenty-seventh. Company officials confirmed the breach on September third, twenty twenty-six.
The attackers exploited a security vulnerability in a self-hosted installation of a software called Metabase. This flaw allowed intruders to obtain administrator access without using a legitimate login.
The compromised files did not include passwords, authentication tokens, academic records, learning activities, or results. Exposed data did not explicitly link user accounts to specific schools. However, investigators noted that attackers might still connect accounts to schools that use identifiable email domains.
Mathspace warned affected individuals to watch for suspicious account activity because criminals may target them using the stolen information.
This security breach is part of a broader cyber campaign. Attackers have recently exploited database vulnerabilities to target other companies, including Trezor, Framework, and Tally.

item.title: From S3 to GPU in One Copy
item.description:
At the QCon London twenty twenty-six conference, SpiralDB maintainer Onur presented Vortex. Vortex is an open-source columnar file format hosted under the Linux Foundation. It is designed to accelerate machine learning data loading from cloud storage like S. three directly to graphics processing units.
When utilizing graphics processing units, systems pay two types of taxes. The first is a movement tax involving multi-step data fetching from S. three into non-volatile memory express disks. It also involves reading compressed bytes into random access memory, central processing unit decompression, and sending decompressed bytes over peripheral component interconnect express to the graphics processing unit.
The second tax is a decision tax occurring when iterating on training workloads by changing filters or data mixes. This traditionally requires full data reprocessing, re-tokenization, and reshuffling. Vortex eliminates these bottlenecks by utilizing lightweight, cascading encodings that allow graphics processing units to handle parallel decompression directly. It also pushes projections, filters, and aggregations down into the file format itself so queries can be modified without full data re-tokenization.
According to the presentation, Vortex storage scans run roughly thirty times faster than Parquet. Its random access speeds are one hundred times or more faster than Parquet. The file format relies on decoupled logical and physical types, fixed-size postscripts, a descriptive footer, and a structure of arrays and layouts. Layouts use zone-maps containing summary statistics like minimum and maximum values. This allows readers to prune unnecessary data segments before performing sliceable compression where only matching row ranges are decompressed.

item.title: Anthropic signed $517bn in compute agreements in past 11 months
item.description: Artificial Intelligence lab Anthropic has signed about five hundred seventeen billion dollars in compute capacity leases over the past eleven months. This comes from an analysis by The Information looking at public announcements and reporting. Since October of last year the company has committed to fourteen point eight gigawatts of compute capacity for the next few years. I., Google Cloud, Lambda, Volta Infra, A. M. D., and Microsoft. item.title: ChatGPT May Soon Learn Your Writing Style From Your Slack or Gmail
item.description:
Open. A. I. is testing a new feature for Chat. G. P. T. It learns your writing style by connecting to external services. These services include Gmail, Slack, Notion, and Google Drive.
The upcoming tool was first spotted on X by, Gael Breton. It was later reported by Bleeping Computer. Breton posted a screenshot that shows a description of how the feature works. The description uses examples from connected apps.
Users who have access can find the option in the settings menu. Look under Personalization and Writing. A toggle reads, Reference my writing style. There is also a prompt to set up the feature.
Open. A. I. has not made an official announcement yet. The company frequently tests new ideas with a small group of users before a wider rollout.
One user replied to the post on X. They said they have had access to the feature for weeks. They described it as a game changer.
It remains unclear how the application processes messages from connected apps. It might process them just once. It might also refer back to them periodically to adapt your style over time.
